memo.verdict: Bullish; progress, to Early-Stage; conviction medium, a working hypothesis until the October 2026 trading update, on which the first direct evidence at the revenue line arrives. The gate does not park the case: management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C, no D or F. The recommendation would move to neutral on the drop-through sensitivity path (a second step in the net finance expense, or no new buyback at the FY2026 results on 4 March 2027). The case would be invalidated by a half-year with Data & Analytics subscription growth below 5% or retention below 92%. Two clean prints with no movement in the multiple would reclassify the case as a 'Compounder' at C rather than a clearing concern at B, and the 'Investment Setup' with it. The record is a Triaging record, v1, dated 2026-09-26; price basis 8,200p on 2026-09-25; ratings snapshot 2026-09-26.
case: - The thesis: LSEG is a high-quality compounder whose shares are priced for a fear the numbers are disproving. At 8,200p the market pays 13.9 times earnings two years out, the bottom of the stock's own ten-year range, for the desktop terminal business to be disintermediated by generative AI; the subscription metrics say it is not being, and the other four-fifths of the group compounds earnings at about 12% a year while the question is settled.

- The change expected is in the evidence about the business, not in the business. The group already grows organically 7% to 8% a year, expands its EBITDA margin about 100bps a year and returns its surplus cash. What changes is whether the numbers reported in October 2026 and March 2027 keep disproving the near-term form of the AI fear; the price already assumes the wrong answer. The fear: Workflows at about 21% of revenue and about 30% of EBITDA on the bear's estimate, growing 2.7% in Q2 2026, with seat growth at 2.9%. The evidence against the fear: annual subscription value 6.1% from 5.9%; retention 92.8% from 92.4%; enterprise agreements 18% of Data & Analytics revenue from 16%; Data & Feeds +7.5% and overtaking Workflows; sales cycles not lengthening while S&P Global's are; real-time traffic +70%; MCP 202 institutions.

- The internal change forces are broad and already in the outputs: guidance raised twice in 2026 on both lines (A); shareholder returns stepped up, £2.1bn in FY2025, £3bn to February 2027, interim dividend +17% (A); standards improving, engineering insourced to 77%, third-party services -15.4%, coding productivity +11%, release velocity +25%, Eikon sunset on time (B); the balance sheet used, leverage 1.8x to 2.1x, JPY 30.5bn notes in August 2026 (B); new products at the fastest cadence since Refinitiv (B); the SwapClear partner-bank share cut from 30% to 15% (FY2025) and 10% (FY2026), extended ten years, worth about 100bps of margin, 2% to 3% of EPS accretion in 2025 (B); other leaders rebuilt and the board refreshed (B); strategy moved from integration to "LSEG Everywhere" with a three-part AI commercial framework in July 2026 (B). Absent: chief-executive change (D), new geographies (D); price rises nominal (C), perimeter moves small (C), no acquisition step-up by design (C). None of the screen's red flags fits. 'Internal forces' B; 'Change Forces' B.
counter_case: - At the 'Investment Thesis' level: LSEG is a "false friend", in the risks report's phrase. The H1 2026 beat was entirely a cost beat (operating expenses £1,882m against consensus £1,919m; revenue only in line) and partly bought by under-investment, capex falling to 8.9% of revenue from 10.2%, the risks report's ninth failure mode being exactly a margin beat stored up as future share loss. The growth in the desktop is price (3.5% ratchets), not seats (2.9% and slowing); Workflows at 2.7% in Q2 2026 is the slowest since Refinitiv. The Refinitiv-era five- to seven-year enterprise deals renew over the next two to three years into procurement teams that cap rises at 0% to 3% and now have AI-native alternatives to price against. The AI monetisation is a framework without a contract, "minimal" in 2026. The EPS growth is bought with buybacks funded by leverage rising from 1.8x to 2.1x in six months, an outlier against peers below 1.5x. The multiple is capped, as Redburn says (Neutral, 10,600p, range-bound), until the AI question is settled, which by Jefferies' own admission cannot be done in the near term. On that reading Morgan Stanley's bear case of 7,538p (a 9% earnings compound rate, divisional multiples five turns lower, Workflows at 17x) is the modal outcome and Jefferies' £65 (zero for Workflows and Risk Intelligence) the tail. The record concedes: the beat was cost-driven; Workflows is a 2% to 3% grower and possibly worse; the buyback is partly debt-funded at the margin; the framework has no revenue attached; the multiple may not move on the first clean print; the risks report's "park" was reasonable on 17 July 2026. The record holds because, first, at 13.9x the market already pays for the false friend and the question is whether the other 79% of revenue (clearing at a 56% segment margin and over 90% share; indices at 67%; feeds growing 7.5%) deserves 14x when its peers trade at 17x to 26x, with Jefferies' £65 sum of the parts saying the disputed businesses are about a fifth of the value and carry no premium; second, the evidence since 17 July runs against the false friend at every operating metric the bear named as an early warning, and the bear's own trigger (subscription growth below 5.0%) is not close; third, equity free cash flow of £2.4bn after £919m of capex, 111% of profit, turns the capital-intensity and non-GAAP items into an accounting note. Where it would abandon the view: a half-year with subscription growth below 5% or retention below 92%; or two clean prints with no movement in the multiple.

- At the 'Foundations' level: the foundation the case leans on, proprietary data, is less defensible than it looks, and the interface is the moat that is eroding. In the sell-side desktop the moat was the workflow and the network, which is why Bloomberg holds 33% to 34% at a rigid price and LSEG concedes 20% to 30%; as AI-native assistants and enterprise data lakes let a bank's own engineers assemble what Workspace assembles, the feed becomes a commodity input priced by procurement, and the enterprise agreements that look like captivity were bought with the flexible, unbundled pricing that makes commoditisation easier. The organisation delivering this has lost a third of its senior managers in three years, scores 74 on engagement, and cannot satisfy its auditor on the subscription-revenue data flows. The record concedes the desktop is and will stay an inferior good, pricing power is nominal, the culture is not an advantage and the control finding lowers confidence in the monitored metric. It holds because vendor consolidation concentrates onto the two largest and LSEG is one; in-house harvesting is deterred by compliance cost and the experts name the aggregators, not the feed owner, as vulnerable; enterprise agreements and retention rose during the very period the bear says commoditisation was under way, and a historic bank merger cost only a one-off £3m in cancellations; and the case needs the subscription line at 5%, not the desktop moat, the desktop being a fifth of revenue growing 2% to 3% inside a division growing 5.2%. It would lose if subscription growth fell below 5% while feeds kept growing.
triggers: - The two dates: the Q3 2026 trading update in October 2026 and the FY2026 results on 4 March 2027 are when the concern clears or does not; the first direct evidence at the revenue line arrives in October.

- Invalidate: a half-year with Data & Analytics subscription growth below 4% (the record's level); the risks report's trigger of below 5.0% and retention below 92% are alarms and the stated abandonment conditions.
- Reclassify: two clean prints without a move in the multiple, which would say the discount is the conglomerate structure, not the AI question, and make the case a 'Compounder' at C.
- The recommendation moves to neutral on the drop-through path: a second step in net finance expense (FY2027 above £330m), or no new buyback announced with the FY2026 results.

- Margin: below +50bps in a year is the alarm; a year of contraction outside the guided H2 2026 lap invalidates the margin driver; capex below the guided 9.5% while release velocity slows would say the beats are bought by under-investment.
- Workflows: growth below 2% or seat growth turning negative; no MCP conversion by Q1 2027; the enterprise-agreement share no longer rising from 18%; Data & Feeds below 6%.
